title: Large personal DOS engine and historical application source discovery
summary: Personally screen 518 candidate URLs and add 15 projects, with 11 explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root assistant personally searched 16 GitHub query routes across Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS; screened 518 unique URLs and reviewed 26 repositories. Fifteen game/application/runtime-source additions and eleven explicit non-promotions. New qualified results skew DOS; no new ST/CPC engine source was invented to fill a quota. Distinguish original decoder/protocol preservation from packer/protocol-port completion; language/mission bytecode VMs from CPU emulation; behavioral native ports from byte-matching binaries; and source-derived continuations from mirrors or binary-only packages. Original-data requirements, private regeneration inputs, encoding issues and unverified builds are explicit. No upstream code, compiler, installer or original binary was executed.

sources.reason: Address-linked combat, world, town, dungeon and intro logic recovered from AVATAR/TITLE with native TypeScript state; original executable is read as data, not executed.
Historical runtime source reconstruction derived from AC 1.14 and AGS legacy sources, with separate instruction-matching stages. Pathfinding source and version directories inspected.
Native ellipsoid-rendering, movement, animation and game modules; same engine reads both games original data and exposes model/scene inspection.
Structured typed mech spawning, scene/task state and mission-chunk interpreter; VM refers to original mission data, not an x86 CPU dispatcher.
Original-author game and level-editor source adapted from Watcom 10.x to Open Watcom 2; inspected DPMI source preserves period interfaces and original author/date.

Annotated IDA disassembly and Ghidra cross-reference plus actual C++ player, entity, resource and renderer modules. Inspected player controller contains structured source, not just planned scaffolding.
Independent C11 rules, original-data extraction and configurable construction kit, derived from executable observations and UnBattletech research.
Author childhood stock-market game recovered from debug-symbol-rich executable; named price-engine and application units are present, preserving original symbols where available.
PCBoard script compiler/decompiler, executable parser and console runtime with actual PPE-command evaluator. Language bytecode VM is not emulation of DOS CPU instructions.
Forty-module symbolic x86 reconstruction with ordered segments and linker references; inspected source still contains mechanical sub_/loc_ symbols.
Readable recovered game modules with typed supply-budget and state accesses, SDL3 platform layer and original-data loaders, rather than CPU/register runtime.
Recovered fixed-point simulation/software renderer compiled to WebAssembly, with named original assembly references and browser adapters.
Hand-rewritten fixed-point tire, drivetrain, collision and traffic physics from DOS/PSX/3DO binaries; inspected formulas retain per-platform address provenance.
Recovered original HDK transmit/receive source preserved with wire-format and transport-boundary documentation.
Official ProPack package mirror retains substantive original method 1/2 unpacker assembly, including inspected 68000 checksum/protected-stream paths and calling convention.
Coursework README records a life-counter address and manipulation notes, but no substantive game-source reconstruction implementation is present. Not promoted as a recovered game.

Solar Realms Elite snapshot overlaps the already tracked formix/sre-re research lineage. The formix repository now returns 404; independent continuation versus mirror is not established. Preserve lineage investigation rather than create another engine entry.
DOS demoscene tribute with reconstruction claims, not a game/application in this focused pass. Keep as a separately scoped demo lead.

README describes a derivative handheld Raptor port, but inspected root lacks textual C/C++ implementation. A binary-release/instructions package does not establish a reviewable new source continuation.
README explicitly describes an inspired new editor, not a complete decompilation or exact clone. Binary-derived algorithm/source evidence was not established for this pass.
Explicit game-specific 68020 interpreter plus AmigaOS/chip HLE running unmodified original executable. Retain architectural audit instead of presenting this as recovered native game source.
New portable CP/M executable compressor with PopCom compatibility, not reconstruction of an original requested-platform application. Modern tooling can be reviewed separately.
Targets PlayStation Forbidden Memories SLUS-01411, not the requested DOS/Amiga/ST/CPC platforms. Do not mistake Windows output platform for original DOS provenance.

Contains genuine recovered-domain work, but reviewed status explicitly retains generated block dispatchers and differential coverage debt. Requires a focused current architecture audit before calling the full game a VM-less high-level source port.

Root currently presents a generic dos_re recovery laboratory plus Ancient Empires knowledge/boot assets, not an established independent native game completion. Preserve specific-game analysis lead without duplicating the tracked framework.
Sid Meiers SimGolf 2002 Windows port, not the earlier DOS SimGolf title. Outside requested source-platform focus regardless of output browser portability.
